sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Gives 36 speakers (1993 census), shift to Sar, and the further-reading citation of Palayer 1975 (pp. 196-219) and the Bua-group bibliography (Boyeldieu 1985 'Présentation sommaire du groupe boua'; Boyeldieu 1983 'Vestiges de suffixes'; Boyeldieu et al. 2018).

sources.note: Nothing; Noy only in Table 1 as '[Lɔɔ or Noy] –' (extinct). No phonology or prosody content.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2018. The Bua Group languages (Chad, Adamawa 13): A comparative perspective. In R. Kramer & R. Kießling (eds), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages (Afrika und Übersee Supplements 34), 53-126. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL halshs-03096908 (author preprint, 58 pp).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere (grep for stress/accent/prosod = 0 hits). Noy appears only as 'Lɔɔ (lɔ́ɔ̄) (or Noy)... extinct' in the inventory (preprint p.2), as 'the then nearly extinct Lɔɔ (Palayer 1975b)' in the documentation outline (p.4), and in fn. 22 (p.11): 'Some of the 43 Lɔɔ words collected by Palayer (1975b) also contain the interior vowels [ə] and [ʉ]'. Sect. 4.4 Tones (p.11-12): 'Ɓa, Lua, Tun, and Bolgo have tone systems with three contrastive heights (Low, Mid, and High), with frequent contour tones'; sect. 5.5 (p.28) says the comparative tone study is 'practically limite…
